events.text: Behind the hall of audience there is a quieter room: shelves of white jade boxes to the ceiling, and an old immortal with ink on her fingers who does not look up. "The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger," she says. "The Court does not sell. It accepts offerings, and it remembers who made them. Stones from below, a little of your standing. Not much stock. It changes when it changes."

choices.text: Ask what she would choose for a family

effects.log: "Pills for the young, a gift for the proud, and patience for yourself," says the Keeper. "The first two I keep on the shelves."

choices.text: Bow to the ledger, as the old immortals do

effects.log: You bow to the open book. The Keeper watches you do it and writes your name a little higher on the page. You are fairly sure that means something.

events.text: A clerk of the Jade Court leads you past three doors that were not there a moment ago. In the last room, a ledger lies open on a lotus of white stone, and every page is a list of names and offerings going back ten thousand years. The Keeper finds a clean line and holds out the brush. "Most immortals come here for themselves," she says. "Write what you came for."

effects.log: The Keeper reads it twice. "That line," she says, "is the rarest in the book." She sets aside the best box on the shelf for you.
"Honest," says the Keeper, and blots it. The ink smells of rain.

events.text: The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger looks at {npc}, who came with you and is trying, with the dignity of fourteen years or more, not to touch the jade boxes, and puts down the brush. "Born up here," says the Keeper. It is not a question. "Children of the clouds grow fast and climb well, if someone feeds them properly. Most parents up here forget how. They have not been children for a very long time."

effects.log: {npc} picks the smallest box on the lowest shelf. Inside is a single sugared petal. The Keeper says it is on the house, which nobody has heard the Keeper say before.

mem.note: chose a box at the Lotus Ledger

choices.text: Ask how to feed a child of the clouds

effects.log: "One pill a year," says the Keeper. "Not more. A body takes in what it takes in. And come here more often than you think you need to."

mem.note: heard you ask how to raise me well
